reading: The top half (above the 5 separator) is a 3x3 pattern drawn at 2x scale; the bottom half is a 6x6 layout. Output is 18x18: the 3x3 pattern is placed in block (r,c) for every non-background layout cell (r,c), other blocks empty.

slots.layout: bottom panel below the separator row (6x6)
slots.placement: 3x3 block at (3r,3c) for each fg layout cell

why: output block (r,c) equals the downscaled pattern iff layout cell (r,c) is fg, else empty

reading: Every isolated 5 is replaced by a 3x3 ring centred on it: 5 at the corners, 1 at the edge midpoints, centre 0.
why: each marker cell becomes the centre of an identical 3x3 unit 515/101/515

reading: Each shape is one colour plus one odd cell whose colour matches one of the grid-corner marker colours. Each shape swaps its two colours, and an overlay of all shapes keyed to a corner colour, drawn entirely in that colour, is pasted into that corner with its box aligned to the corner.
verb: swap colours and collect to corner

slots.shapes: objects with one main colour and one odd cell
slots.key: corner cell colours of the grid
slots.swap: main colour <-> odd-cell colour inside each shape
slots.corner copy: union of shapes whose odd colour = corner colour, in that colour, aligned to that corner

why: every shape's colours are swapped in place and each corner holds the union silhouette of its shapes

reading: A lattice of framed tiles; a few tiles have a rare centre colour. Background gap cells on a row or column lying between two cells of the same rare colour are filled with that colour, linking those tiles; tiles themselves are unchanged.

new_rows.name: link
new_rows.datalog:
pcount(C, count(Y, X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
more(C, D) :- pcount(C, N), pcount(D, M), M > N.
nmore(C, count(D)) :- more(C, D).
special(C) :- nmore(C, K), K >= 3.
zero(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, B), B = 0.
hlink(Y, X) :- zero(Y, X), px(Y, X1, C), special(C), px(Y, X2, C), X1 < X, X < X2.
vlink(Y, X) :- zero(Y, X), px(Y1, X, C), special(C), px(Y2, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.
link(Y, X) :- hlink(Y, X).
link(Y, X) :- vlink(Y, X).

why: every changed cell is a 0 cell flanked on its row or column by two cells of one rare colour (a colour with at least 3 more frequent colours), and takes that colour

reading: The grid is symmetric under both mirror axes; blocks painted with noise colour 4 are restored from their mirror images.
why: the output is symmetric about the central vertical and horizontal axes and contains no 4

reading: A bottom-row cup has outer colour A and inner colour B with a cap of A above. From each top corner of the cap a diagonal ray of colour B goes up and outward to the grid border.

slots.source: the two ends of the topmost fg row (the cap)
slots.direction: diagonally up-left and up-right, starting one step beyond the cap ends
slots.colour: the inner (minority) colour of the bottom shape

why: every new cell lies on one of the two diagonals from the cap ends and has the inner colour

reading: Panels separated by full lines each hold the same small shape, shifted vertically by a constant step from panel to panel. The output is a single panel with the shape at the next position of the progression.

slots.panels: stripes cut by full separator columns
slots.shape: the small object in each panel
slots.step: vertical offset between shapes in consecutive panels
slots.output: one panel (with its border) with the shape placed at the next step after the last panel

why: output is one panel; its shape is the panel shape translated vertically along the progression (the second pair lands one row further than a strict constant step)

reading: Every 4 in a column whose index is a multiple of 3 (0, 3, 6, ...) becomes 6.

new_rows.name: third
new_rows.datalog:
col3(X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
col3(X2) :- col3(X), X2 = X + 3, px(Y, X2, C).
third(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0, col3(X).

why: cells with colour 4 in columns 0 mod 3 map 4 -> 6; nothing else changes

reading: Two 4x4 panels split by a 5 column. If the right panel's coloured cells exactly cover the left panel's background cells at the same positions, the output is the left panel with them filled in; otherwise the output is the left panel unchanged.

slots.panels: left and right panels cut by the separator column
slots.test: right fg cell set == left bg cell set, position for position (no shifting)
slots.yes: left panel overlaid with right panel

why: output equals left panel overlaid with right exactly when they are complementary, else the left panel

reading: Two 2 markers lie on a common row, column or diagonal. The straight line joining them is drawn: background cells on it become 2 and 1 cells on it become 3.

slots.line: cells on the straight (orthogonal or diagonal) segment between them

why: every changed cell lies on the segment joining the two 2s; off-line cells are unchanged
